Okay, it's spooky season, which means it's our season! For anyone new: I run Eldergulch Audio out of a tiny basement studio in Denver. Our show, The Eldergulch Tapes, is a fictional horror audio drama about an old Colorado mining town that just stopped existing one winter. Season 3 is the creepiest one yet. We recorded part of it in a real abandoned tunnel up near Idaho Springs, and our sound engineer still won't talk about the take where something answered back.

Here's the copy from our landing page:
"The Eldergulch Tapes is a fictional horror audio drama about a Colorado mining town that went silent in 1893, told through the recordings it left behind. Season 3, "The Long Shaft," drops one new episode every night through Halloween: eight episodes, all free to stream on Spotify, Apple Podcasts or any podcast app. Free for listeners anywhere in the United States. Lights off, headphones on."

The page is https://eldergulch.com/season3 and it links out to all the listening apps.

The details:
- Run the campaign from Sunday, October 24, 2027 through Sunday, October 31, 2027 (Halloween night), on Mountain Time, our time here in Denver.
- What I care about is streams, meaning people actually opening the new season on a streaming service. Get us as many of those as you can. Streams are what we count.
- One catch: we don't have X's pixel on the site, so X can't see when someone streams. We read the numbers from the podcast platforms ourselves.
- You don't need to check with me. Launch it and manage it however you think is best.
- Please keep an eye on it the whole week while it runs.
- When it wraps, send me a short recap with spend, impressions and link clicks.

Thanks so much. I'll be over here hiding from my own show.

Total budget: 700.00 USD for everything you launch: every campaign and ad group draws on this one budget. We've approved these 4 posts, all on our account, and only these, so please don't write new ones. Promote whichever you think will work, in as many campaigns and ad groups as you like, and change, pause or stop them as you learn what works:
